You get **28 days of holiday a year, plus public holidays**.

SOURCE: docs/people/holiday.md

Up to five unused holiday days carry over to the next year.

SOURCE: docs/people/holiday.md

You need a doctor's note after seven calendar days of sickness absence. Full pay continues for 20 working days in any rolling year.

SOURCE: docs/people/sick-leave.md (acme-handbook)

You have **30 days** from the date you spent the money to submit your expense claim in the expenses tool.

SOURCE: docs/people/expenses.md (acme-handbook)

If your laptop is lost or stolen, tell the IT desk within one hour so it can be wiped. Raise every other equipment request through the IT portal.

SOURCE: docs/it/laptops.md (acme-handbook), owner IT, trust: "Written by its owner. Not checked against anything."

The catalog only surfaces a document titled "Paying suppliers" (`docs/finance/invoices.md`, Finance, trust: "Written by its owner. Not checked against anything.") whose excerpt is just "How supplier invoices get paid." — it does not include the actual requirements for getting a supplier invoice paid. No other tool result contained that detail.

NOT FOUND

According to the handbook (`docs/legal/nda.md`, owned by Legal):

- **Only directors can sign contracts.**
- Anything worth more than **£50,000** also needs **legal review**.

SOURCE: docs/legal/nda.md

The primary brand colour is **Acme teal** (per `docs/marketing/brand.md` in the `acme-handbook` repo, owned by Marketing).

SOURCE: docs/marketing/brand.md

Sales can offer up to **15 percent** without approval. Anything deeper needs sign-off from the head of sales.

SOURCE: docs/product/pricing.md (acme-handbook)

The available tools only returned a short excerpt for the incident communications policy ("Who says what, to whom, during a customer-visible incident.") and did not include any update cadence or frequency. I could not retrieve the full document content, so I can't confirm how often updates are posted during an incident.

NOT FOUND

The acquirer's idempotency window for replaying captures is **24 hours**. Captures older than that are re-authorised rather than replayed, and re-authorisation requires a customer-facing decision.

SOURCE: docs/ops/replay.md (payments-service)

The catalog only surfaces the title of `docs/daily-reconciliation.md` (owned by Data Platform in the `reporter` repo); its excerpt contains no schedule or run time, and no other result mentions when the daily reconciliation report runs.

NOT FOUND

A payment gets stuck in `capturing` when its status is `capturing` but no capture task is running — per the "Capturing a payment" flow (declared, evidence checked 2026-11-06), the stuck sign is exactly "status is capturing and no capture task is running," with recovery pointing to `docs/runbook.md`.

A draft finding (hypothesis, not established fact) — "Investigating a capture potentially stuck in capturing" (`docs/findings/capture-stuck-after-worker-restart.md`) — suggests one scenario: a payment stayed in `capturing` after the worker restarted. That is a hypothesis, not confirmed cause.

To recover, the "Re-running a stuck capture" flow (declared, evidence checked 2026-11-06) has an operator set the payment's status from `capturing` to `captured` (via operator) so a new capture task can start; per that flow, "No money has moved."

SOURCE: flows/capturing-a-payment.md (and flows/re-running-a-capture.md; docs/findings/capture-stuck-after-worker-restart.md is a draft hypothesis)

Nobody has written down a parental leave policy in the company knowledge base. The closest documents are "Holiday and time off" (`docs/people/holiday.md`) and "Sickness absence" (`docs/people/sick-leave.md`), both owned by People, but neither covers parental leave.

SOURCE: NOT FOUND

Nobody has written this down. The tools contain no information about a company pension contribution.

NOT FOUND

Based on my searches, nothing in the available tools covers salary bands for engineers. Nobody has written this down.

SOURCE: NOT FOUND
